result.summary: The landlord says his plumber fixed the no-hot-water / no-boiler-power fault on 14 May. He only knows this from a text from the plumber, and the tenant hasn't confirmed it. She also mentioned a letterbox fault on 13 May, which still has no details. I sent the tenant one SMS asking her to confirm whether hot water is back and to describe the letterbox fault. I also placed a hold with a follow-up on 19 May. I'm not closing the ticket until the tenant confirms the repair.
result.situation: This is a landlord-managed repair (events 007 and 010). The tenant reported no hot water and no power at the boiler on 6 May. The landlord's contractor didn't come for over a week (events 012, 015, 017). On 15 May the landlord said his plumber attended on 14 May and fixed it, going only on the plumber's text, with no report (event 018). Maya asked the tenant to confirm by voicemail and email on 15 May (events 019 and 020) and got no reply. The tenant also raised a letterbox fault on 13 May (event 017), and nobody has followed it up. There was no hold or follow-up on the ticket.

actions_taken.description: Loaded the ticket, profiles and the 21 events
actions_taken.result: Stage intake, no holds, approvals or attachments, empty profiles

actions_taken.description: Looked for past lessons on unconfirmed landlord-reported fixes
SMS to the tenant (her email from 15 May got no reply). Asked whether the boiler, shower and taps work now, and asked for letterbox details and a photo. Said we will follow up on 19 May.
Hold waiting on the tenant's confirmation and letterbox details
Landlord: uses his own contractors, and agreed the agency may send its own if his doesn't come
Tenant: wants to be contacted herself about access; the household member at home doesn't speak English

escalation.reason: The tenant can answer the open question. Nothing is in dispute and nothing needs agency judgement yet.
escalation.recommendation: At follow-up: if the tenant says hot water still isn't working, or doesn't reply, tell the landlord and use his offer from event 015 for the agency to send a Gas Safe engineer (or an electrician, if it's a power fault) quickly. Escalate if hot water has now been out for more than 2 weeks. If she confirms it's fixed, close the hot-water job and open the letterbox job separately.

judgement.why_this_decision: The only evidence that the fault is fixed is the landlord passing on a text from his plumber (event 018). Before that, the tenant said three times that nothing had been done (events 012, 017). The tenant is the person who can confirm the repair, so closing now would rest on hearsay. The letterbox fault from event 017 was never followed up, so I combined both questions into one message. I used SMS because her email from 15 May got no reply.

alternatives_considered.option: Close the ticket on the landlord's word
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord's report is second-hand, with no work report, and the tenant hasn't confirmed.

alternatives_considered.option: Send the agency's own contractor now
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord says it's fixed. Sending someone before the tenant confirms the fault is still there could waste the landlord's money.
The tenant can answer this herself. She has only been chased once since the landlord's update, about 1.3 days ago.
There was no hold, and the letterbox report had gone unanswered. Leaving it would let the case go silent.

Attachments: none visible (no plumber report or invoice)
Letterbox: no details or assessment recorded
assumptions: SMS should reach the tenant. Contact details aren't in the CRM, so the team routes outbox messages

The cause of the boiler power loss and whether any electrical or gas checks were done
risks_or_red_flags: The tenant may have been without hot water for 8+ days (6 to 14 May), or longer if it isn't fixed
The landlord's contractor didn't attend several times when promised
There is no record of the repair or the checks done on a boiler that lost power
The household member at home doesn't speak English, so access needs to be arranged through the tenant
result.final_status: Open, stage intake, on hold (276) waiting for the tenant's reply

next_follow_up.what: Check the tenant's reply. If hot water is back, close the hot-water job and scope the letterbox fault. If not, or if she hasn't replied, tell the landlord and arrange the agency's contractor as he offered in event 015, escalating if needed.
